newsitem.title: GERMANY: Volvo Trucks sees brighter Americas.
newsitem.headline: Volvo Trucks sees brighter Americas.

text.p: Volvo Trucks said on Thursday that it could see its loss making operations in the U.S. reaching a break-even point although no date was given.

"Yes, we will reach break-even in North America but whether it happens in June, July or some other month, I see as less important," Volvo Truck's managing director Karl-Erling Trogen told a seminar in Frankfurt.
"We have made significant improvements on the American market and the improvements are continuing."
Trogen said Volvo Truck's market share in North America reached 10 percent in February this year compared to 9.1 percent in 1996.
"This year our market share will be about 12 percent," he said.

"In the longterm 12 percent is not really adequate. We are working hard to raise the market share further but I don't want to go into any more details and don't want to give away too much to our competitors."
He said Volvo was working hard to reduce costs in North America. Among other things the number of employees had been cut in the past seven to eight months to 2,715 from 3,500.
Trogen said Volvo Truck had returned to profitability in South America this year.
"We have dragged down the cost base and today we have a profitable operation in South America," he said.
